extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students studying algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook chapter material and exercise guidance for understanding the sheaf/module of differentials (Ω), its universal property, exact sequences (relative cotangent, conormal, Euler), behavior under base change, and the definition/criteria for smoothness and related invariants (canonical bundle, geometric genus, Hodge numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification that a map d is a derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: To check d is a derivation one shows d is B-linear and satisfies the Leibniz rule: d(aa') = a d(a') + a' d(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text checks B-linearity explicitly and writes out the Leibniz check step-by-step. This is the canonical verification when showing a proposed map defines a derivation or differential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal property of Ω_{A/B} and induced morphism Ω_{A/B} → I/I^2 (Theorem 21.2.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural morphism f : Ω_{A/B} → I/I^2 induced by the universal property of Ω_{A/B}; Theorem 21.2.24 states this morphism is an isomorphism (when appropriate hypotheses hold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy given: (i) show f is surjective by checking images of generators, (ii) construct g : I/I^2 → Ω_{A/B} (via x ↦ x dy type maps) and check g annihilates I^2 so is well-defined, then show g◦f = identity. The text includes the explicit algebraic manipulations and Leibniz-rule uses needed to verify well-definedness and injectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing of afﬁne differentials to global sheaf (identification on opens)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a morphism of schemes and Spec A ⊂ X with π−1(Spec B), then Γ(Spec A, Ω_{X/Y}) identifies with Ω_{A/B}; the global construction 'glues together' the affine constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.2.N suggests identifying Γ(Spec A, Ω_{X/Y}) with Ω_{A/B}. The textbook emphasizes that understanding Ω on affine opens lets one generalize statements to non-affine settings; proofs frequently proceed by checking compatibly on affine covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence of Ω_{X/Y}
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is locally of finite type and Y (hence X) is locally Noetherian, then Ω_{X/Y} is a coherent sheaf on X (Exercise 21.2.P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may weaken Noetherian hypotheses for weaker conclusions. The exercise asks to show coherence using the affine description and standard finiteness arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local freeness of Ω_{X/Y} for smooth relative dimension n
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is smooth of relative dimension n, then Ω_{X/Y} is locally free (a vector bundle) of rank n (Exercise 21.2.Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use Jacobian description of Ω (Exercise 21.2.E). This is the standard criterion that for smooth morphisms the sheaf of relative differentials is a rank-n locally free sheaf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative cotangent exact sequence (Theorem 21.2.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For morphisms X → Y → Z there is an exact sequence of quasi-coherent sheaves on X: π^*Ω_{Y/Z} → Ω_{X/Z} → Ω_{X/Y} → 0, globalizing the affine version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exact sequence is the sheafified/global version of the algebraic relative cotangent sequence and is used to relate differentials across composable morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conormal exact sequence for closed embeddings (Theorem 21.2.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If i : X ↪ Y is a closed embedding with conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/Y}, and Y → Z is a morphism, then there is an exact sequence of sheaves on X: N^∨_{X/Y} → i^*Ω_{Y/Z} → Ω_{X/Z} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This globalizes the affine conormal exact sequence (Theorem 21.2.12). It is a standard tool for relating infinitesimal deformation data of a subvariety to ambient differentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness of the relative cotangent sequence under smoothness
rubrics_metrics.description: The relative cotangent exact sequence is exact on the left if the involved morphisms (π and ρ) are smooth (Exercise 21.2.S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use a block upper-triangular matrix argument (compare to Exercise 12.6.D). In practice smoothness hypotheses upgrade right-exact sequences to short exact sequences on the left as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of differentials and base change compatibility (Theorem 21.2.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a cartesian square X' → X over Y' → Y there is a natural homomorphism μ^*Ω_{X/Y} → Ω_{X'/Y'}; if the square is Cartesian (X' ≅ X×_Y Y') this map is an isomorphism (Ω behaves well under base change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (a) records existence of the pullback map in general; part (b) gives the base-change isomorphism. Exercise 21.2.T suggests deriving this from the affine/exercise construction and gluing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiberwise compatibility: fiber of Ω is differentials of the fiber
rubrics_metrics.description: As a consequence of base change compatibility, the fiber of the sheaf of relative differentials equals the sheaf of differentials of the geometric fiber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies thinking of Ω_{X/Y} as a family of cotangent spaces varying over Y; many arguments reduce to checking at fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redefinition/criterion for k-smoothness (21.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A k-scheme X is k-smooth of dimension n if it is locally of finite type, of pure dimension n, and Ω_{X/k} is locally free of rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the robust definition used going forward; exercises (21.3.A etc.) ask the reader to verify equivalence with earlier definitions. One may call a scheme smooth if it's a disjoint union of smooth pieces of varying dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking smoothness on affine covers via the Jacobian criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Smoothness can be checked on any affine cover by applying the Jacobian criterion on each affine open (Observation 21.3.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces many checks of smoothness to explicit computations in rings/algebras on affine charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: smoothness vs regularity at closed points over perfect fields
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is perfect and X is finite type over k, then X is smooth iff X is regular at all closed points (Exercise 21.3.D and remark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a practical criterion: for varieties over perfect fields, verifying regularity at closed points suffices to conclude smoothness. Hints reference base change to perfect closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness theorem (21.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an irreducible variety over a perfect field k of dimension n, there is a dense open subset U ⊂ X such that U is smooth of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: check rank of Ω at the generic point equals n, then use upper semicontinuity of rank of coherent sheaves. Uses separable generation of transcendence-degree-n extensions over perfect fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness of conormal sequence for embeddings of smooth varieties (Theorem 21.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed embedding i : X ↪ Y of smooth k-varieties with conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/Y}, the conormal exact sequence is exact on the left: 0 → N^∨_{X/Y} → i^*Ω_{Y/k} → Ω_{X/k} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses that X is regular at closed points (hence a regular embedding), Proposition 21.2.16(b) on I/I^2, and checks at associated/generic points; dualizing gives the normal exact sequence of tangent sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader exactness conditions for conormal sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The conormal sequence is exact on the left under more general 'appropriate smoothness' hypotheses (see Stacks project tags 06B7 and 06BB) beyond the case of smooth varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to Stacks project indicates the general technical conditions under which left-exactness holds; the textbook points out practical sufficient smoothness hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Zariski cotangent space with fiber of Ω at separable closed point (Corollary 21.3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is a smooth k-variety and q ∈ Y is a closed point whose residue field κ(q) is separable over k, then the conormal exact sequence for q ↪ Y yields an isomorphism of the Zariski cotangent space at q with the fiber of Ω_{Y/k} at q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends earlier results (e.g., Proposition 21.2.18) to separable closed points, and provides a concrete identification used to compute tangent/cotangent spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric genus of a curve via Ω (21.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a regular irreducible projective curve C over k, the geometric genus is h^0(C, Ω_{C/k}) (the space of global differentials); this is finite because Ω_{C/k} is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The geometric genus equals first algebraic de Rham cohomology; Exercise 21.5.C relates this to earlier genus definitions h^1(C, O_C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation: Ω_{P^1/k} ≅ O(-2) (21.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: On P^1_k the sheaf of differentials Ω_{P^1/k} is isomorphic to O(-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: take dx on one patch, transform to the other patch where it acquires a double pole; argument works over Z as well and base-change (Theorem 21.2.27(b)) gives Ω_{P^1_B/B} ≅ O(-2) for any base scheme B. This example illustrates using local coordinates and tracking zeros/poles to identify line bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for computing differentials and geometric genus on hyperelliptic curves (Exercises 21.4.A–C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a hyperelliptic curve C given as a double cover π: C → P^1 branched at 2g+2 points, compute π^*dx, count zeros and poles to find deg Ω_{C/k} = 2g-2, and produce explicit differentials ω_i = x^i dx/y to show h^0(C, Ω_{C/k}) = g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises guide through showing dx is regular on the affine chart, determining valuations at branch points and infinity, proving linear independence of ω_i and that they form a basis; also guides toward Serre duality interpretations via residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentials of discrete valuation rings are free of rank one (Exercise 21.4.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A, m, k) is a DVR that is a localization of a finitely generated k-algebra, and t is a uniformizer, then Ω_{A/k} ≅ A·dt (free rank 1 generated by dt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested proof steps: show Ω_{A/k} finitely generated, exhibit a surjection from A·dt to Ω and use Nakayama, then show dt is non-torsion by specializing to A/(t^N) ≅ k[t]/(t^N). The exercise also indicates generalizations to regular local rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler exact sequence for projective space (Theorem 21.4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: On projective space P^n_A over a ring A there is an exact sequence: 0 → Ω_{P^n_A/A} → O(-1)^{⊕(n+1)} → O → 0 (and dualizing gives a sequence describing the tangent bundle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of the map φ: O(-1)^{⊕(n+1)} → O(0) is given explicitly by (s_0,...,s_n) ↦ Σ x_i s_i; proof reduces to checking on standard affine patches D(x_i) and matching homogeneous degree conditions. Exercises guide verification of surjectivity and identification of the kernel with Ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizations of the Euler sequence (relative projective bundles and Grassmannians)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a rank-(n+1) locally free sheaf V on X, Ω_{P(V)/X} fits into an Euler sequence 0 → Ω_{P(V)/X} → O(-1) ⊗ π^*V^∨ → O_{P(V)} → 0; for Grassmannians G(m,n+1) one has Ω_{G(m,n+1)/k} ≅ Hom(Q, S) where 0 → S → V → Q → 0 is the tautological exact sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These generalizations are stated and exercises (21.4.H–I) ask the reader to verify the special cases and prove the Grassmannian identification; they are useful for understanding normal bundles and deformation theory of subvarieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of i-forms Ω^i_{X/Y} and birational invariance of H^0(X, Ω^i) for smooth projective varieties (21.5.1, 21.5.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Ω^i_{X/Y} := ∧^i Ω_{X/Y}. If X and X' are birational irreducible smooth projective k-varieties, then for each i, H^0(X, Ω^i_{X/k}) ≅ H^0(X', Ω^i_{X'/k}) (Exercise 21.5.A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: pull back i-forms via the birational map on its domain, use Algebraic Hartogs lemma to extend across codimension ≥2 complement, and check inverse rational map gives inverse on global sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical bundle K_X and geometric genus p_g(X) (21.5.3–21.5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a smooth n-dimensional k-variety X, the canonical bundle K_X is det Ω_{X/k} = Ω^n_{X/k}. For projective smooth X the geometric genus p_g(X) is defined as h^0(X, K_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text remarks K_X is the algebraic volume form sheaf and connects p_g to other invariants (e.g., for curves p_g = h^1(C, O_C)). Exercises (21.5.B, 21.5.C) give adjunction and relationships to arithmetic genus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of Fano, Calabi–Yau, plurigenera and Kodaira dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: X is Fano if K_X^∨ is isomorphic to O_X; Calabi–Yau if K_X is trivial (suitably interpreted); the jth plurigenus h^0(X, K_X^{⊗j}) is a birational invariant for j ≥ 0, and the Kodaira dimension κ(X) measures growth of plurigenera (κ = -1 if all plurigenera are 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises ask to compute these invariants for complete intersections and curves. The text notes plurigenera are birational invariants (Exercise 21.5.E) and explains how Kodaira dimension ranges between -1 and dim X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kodaira vanishing theorem (statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If k has characteristic 0 and X is a smooth projective k-variety and L is an ample invertible sheaf, then H^i(X, K_X ⊗ L) = 0 for i > 0 (Kodaira vanishing, 21.5.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text remarks the char 0 restriction is necessary (Raynaud counterexamples in positive characteristic) and sketches historical proofs (analytic proof via GAGA, Lefschetz principle reductions) and references for algebraic proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hodge numbers and basic properties (21.5.10–21.5.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Hodge numbers h^{i,j}(X) = dim H^j(X, Ω^i_{X/k}). For smooth projective varieties over k = k, h^{i,0} are birational invariants; Serre duality gives symmetry h_{p,q} = h_{n-p,n-q}, and over C one has the Hodge decomposition H^m(X, C) = ⊕_{i+j=m} H^j(X, Ω^i_{X/C}) and complex-conjugation symmetry h^{i,j} = h^{j,i}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises (21.5.L, 21.5.M) ask to prove Serre-duality symmetries and compute Hodge numbers for projective space via the Euler sequence. The text warns some additional symmetries may fail in positive characteristic and gives references.
